findings.summary: the final JSON assertion requires two plugin entries after the fixture is reset to one Claude user installation and Copilot has been removed, so the specified implementation cannot pass

the gate removes copilot.exe even on macOS, where its own harness installs the fake agent as copilot, causing a missing-file failure after the behaviour is implemented rather than a product assertion failure
the T5 gate runs T3's gate first, so the one-entry fixture assertion expecting two entries makes a correct final implementation fail before T5's own worked example runs

notes: All five gates were rerun with vloop task gate; on the base each failed at the expected missing behaviour assertion. Criterion judges by acceptance order: T1 1 gate; 2 gate; 3 gate plus review for absence of lookup; 4 gate; 5 gate; 6 gate plus review; 7 gate; 8 gate plus review; 9 go check and review; 10 T4 gate and review; 11 review and go check. T2 1 gate; 2 gate; 3 gate plus review for both Windows failures; 4 review of committed failure-path tests; 5 gate; 6 go check and review; 7 review. T3 1 gate and review; 2 gate; 3 gate and review; 4 gate and review; 5 gate; 6 gate; 7 go check and review; 8 review. T4 1 gate; 2 gate and review; 3 gate; 4 gate; 5 gate; 6 review; 7 go check and review. T5 1 go check and review; 2 go check and review; 3 T5 gate; 4 go check and review. The T3 count was checked against the literal fixture and is 1, while the assertion expects 2. The plan declares macOS and Windows; the T3 copilot.exe removal is host-specific and is therefore unpassable there.
